target.title: fix(twilio): redact webhook turnToken diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary
- Redacts query parameter values from failed Twilio webhook verification diagnostics before they are returned to the Twilio provider adapter and logged.
- Keeps Twilio signature verification and replay keys on the original full verification URL for valid requests; only failed diagnostic output is redacted.
- Collision check: searched open PRs for `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.ts`, `extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio/webhook.ts`, `turnToken`, and Twilio verification URL redaction; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found. This is a targeted diagnostic redaction fix, not a P1/severity escalation claim.

## Verification
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  2 passed (2)`, `Tests  55 passed (55)`.
- Mutation check: temporarily returning the original URL from `redactTwilioVerificationUrlForDiagnostics` made both new tests fail because `turnToken=secret-turn-token` reached the failed verification reason and Twilio warning logs; restoring the redaction returned the focused tests to green.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.test.ts` - passed; exit 0. The normal prepare phase was attempted but hung in `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mjs`, so I reran oxlint with the repository's documented skip-prepare environment after dependencies were installed.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: failed Twilio webhook verification logs should not disclose `turnToken` or other callback query parameter values while preserving full URL verification for valid signatures.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout using the real exported `verifyTwilioProviderWebhook` adapter path. No mocks were used in this proof command; the adapter emitted its normal `console.warn` diagnostics.

Exact command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with an inline script that calls `verifyTwilioProviderWebhook` for an invalid Twilio signature on `https://example.com/voice/twilio?callId=call-1&turnToken=secret-turn-token`.

Evidence after fix:

```text
[twilio] Webhook verification failed: Invalid signature for URL: https://example.com/voice/twilio?callId=***&turnToken=***
[twilio] Verification URL: https://example.com/voice/twilio?callId=***&turnToken=***
result_ok=false
reason_contains_secret=false
reason_contains_redaction=true
```

Observed result after fix: failed verification still fails closed, but both warning lines redact query values and the returned reason does not contain the original `secret-turn-token`.

What was not tested: no live Twilio webhook delivery was used; this proof exercises the OpenClaw Twilio verification adapter locally with deterministic signed-input fixtures.
